text:
maya_support: FYI ACME (acme_integration) opened an escalation — their chat assistant started returning shorter, differently-structured answers after yesterday's runtime rollout. They say it correlates with a change in how our chat templates are applied.

acme_integration: we noticed a ~15% drop in the presence of the safety header in replies and some JSON outputs are now invalid (missing trailing commas/fields). This started after your most recent deploy. Example request/response attached.

maya_support: attaching the customer's minimal repro below (they gave this exact body).

acme_integration: ```json
{
  "model": "redwood-large-v1",
  "input": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant.\n\nPlease always include a \"source\" field."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Summarize the following: \"Q: What's the refund policy? A: Refunds processed in 7 days.\""}
  ]
}
```

acme_integration: expected SUMMARY with a source field, actual response lacked the source key and truncated the last sentence.

deploy-bot: rolled out chat-template-normalization v2.3.1 -> normalized whitespace in all system messages (strip trailing/leading spaces/newlines). rollout started 1837651200, completed 1837653000. commit: 9f4b2a0.

eli_sre: tagging @jia_ml since this looks like ML/template interaction. I pulled the request logs — nothing errored in infra. Latency/throughput normal.

jia_ml: I can repro locally. The normalization removes the trailing double-newline that used to separate system and user blocks; that changes tokenization around the boundary. With the extra newline the tokenizer emits a separate newline token that the model learned to interpret as 'end-of-system' marker and trigger the source field. Removing it collapses tokens and the model's output distribution shifts.

jia_ml: repro steps I used:
```
# curl snippet
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large-v1","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant.\\n\\nPlease always include a \"source\" field."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize: ..."}]}'
```
Output A (with trailing \n\n in system): `{ "summary": "Refunds processed in 7 days.", "source": "policy/returns" }`
Output B (normalized): `{ "summary": "Refunds processed in 7 days." }`

jia_ml: tokenizer diffs (hex-level) show different subtoken boundaries near the quotes/newline. This is small but the model is brittle to this particular marker.

eli_sre: do we have a quick mitigation? rollback the normalization? or patch templates to inject explicit token that is preserved after normalization?

sam_prod: product note — changing model behavior even slightly is a regression for customers who rely on deterministic structure. We should prefer a conservative approach. Sam -> agrees rollback unless ML has a safe patch.

jia_ml: two options: 1) rollback the normalization rollout (fast, global) 2) adjust the runtime to canonicalize system->user boundary into an explicit sentinel token (e.g., "<SYS_END>") that is added *after* normalization (safer long-term). Option 2 needs ~1-2 days dev work and careful QA across templates.

maya_support: customer asks for ETA and whether they should expect lost data or billing impacts. They also shared a few more failing examples I can forward if needed.

eli_sre: rolling back v2.3.1 now would stop new incidents. If we take that route we need a postmortem and new rollout checklist to include regression-e2e on structured-output customers.

deploy-bot: rollback job queued: rollback chat-template-normalization v2.3.1 -> target 1837654600. Initiated by eli_sre? Confirm.

sam_prod: confirm rollback ASAP. Also we should add a short-term mitigation: for dedicated/private customers allow a compatibility flag that preserves original spacing for system messages. That can be a config toggle while we design sentinel approach.

jia_ml: I'll prototype sentinel insertion today and run a small regression harness against the customer's prompt set. If green I'll coordinate a canary. Owner: jia_ml. ETA: prototype + tests by EOD -> canary 24-48h.

maya_support: telling ACME: we will rollback normalization immediately and follow up with a patch plan and ETA. Sorry for the disruption. 

acme_integration: thanks — please share when rollback is done and any temp workaround. This impacted production in a few chats. :pray:

eli_sre: action items: [rollback v2.3.1] (assigned eli_sre, now), [compat flag for spacing] (sam_prod + eng-infra), [sentinel design + tests] (jia_ml), [customer postmortem summary] (maya_support).

maya_support: I'll collect the customer's failing prompts and attach to the incident after rollback.

jia_ml: one more note — this is a good reminder that whitespace changes are not semantics-free for LLMs. We should add a regression test that includes boundary-sensitive prompts (function-calling, JSON templates, structured outputs).

sam_prod: agreed. Adding to roadmap / prioritization.

eli_sre: rollback confirmed scheduled. I'll post when completed.

deploy-bot: rollback chat-template-normalization v2.3.1 -> executed 1837654475, status: started.

maya_support: thanks all. will update ACME after deploy-bot confirms finished.

deploy-bot: rollback chat-template-normalization v2.3.1 -> completed 1837654498, status: success.

acme_integration: verified — behavior back to previous outputs. Thank you.

maya_support: closing loop with the customer and starting postmortem doc.

jia_ml: will follow up with PR for sentinel approach and test harness link.

sam_prod: add a note to release runbook: "don’t change template whitespace without structured-output regression checks." :memo:
